claims.text: Local atomic-size mismatch and resulting lattice strain control superconducting transition temperature in HEA superconductors outside Nb-Ta and titanium-rich systems.
Lattice strain modulates the density of states at the Fermi level.
Electron-phonon coupling and the density of states at the Fermi level modulate Tc.
Substitution with isoelectronic elements having substantially different atomic radii can vary local atomic-size mismatch while preserving electron count.
Changing local atomic-size mismatch through isoelectronic substitution will change induced lattice strain.
The proposed substitutions can vary lattice strain while keeping the crystal structure constant.
Perturbation of lattice dynamics by increased strain may enhance electron-phonon coupling up to an optimum.
Beyond an optimum strain level, disorder may degrade superconductivity.
Substitution with larger-radius elements will increase local lattice strain relative to the baseline.
Increasing local lattice strain will produce a systematic change in Tc relative to the baseline alloy.
The measured degree of induced strain will correlate with shifts in Tc.
Defect-induced scattering or changes in phonon dispersion may obscure the relationship between strain and Tc.
The hypothesis is restricted to single-phase solid solutions containing at least five elements at concentrations of at least 5 at.% each, with constant electron count and crystal structure.
A lack of a systematic or statistically significant strain-Tc correlation would falsify the hypothesis.
